correctness.rationale: Equivariance requires a union of full source orbits, maps them injectively to complete target orbits, and permits exactly one of ell shifts on each paired orbit. Dividing by full rank gives the stated falling-factorial weights. The summable majorant for bounded m/ell proves pointwise and total-variation convergence after normalization. At R=sqrt(m/ell) with R/m tending to zero, the successive ratio is uniformly separated from 1 on the two indicated buffered sides; comparing each exterior boundary to an interior weight by Theta(R) such ratios and summing the exterior geometric series gives the claimed concentration. Independently enumerating partial endofunction arrays with an undefined sentinel, deleting arrays with repeated defined images, and checking commutation gave rank counts (1,8,8) at ranks (0,2,4) for (m,ell)=(2,2), (1,12,18) at (0,3,6) for (2,3), and (1,18,72,48) at (0,2,4,6) for (3,2); omitted ranks had count zero. This finite check supports the coefficient identity only.

evidence: DLMF 18.11.6, citing Szegő, Theorem 8.22.4, states that L_m(x/m) converges to J_0(2 sqrt(x)) for alpha=0, uniformly on bounded complex x-sets.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Taking x=-(m/ell)z gives the numerator uniformly on compact z-sets when m/ell tends to lambda in [0,infinity); at z=1 the limit is positive. The resulting generating-function limit is the whole claimed critical law, and at lambda=0 it gives the mass-one-at-zero case. This theorem does not claim uniformity at diverging x.

originality.rationale: The central novelty claim is the critical Bessel crossover rather than the credited finite count. The entire critical probability generating function is a ratio of ordinary Laguerre polynomials to which the classical complex-uniform Mehler–Heine theorem applies immediately. This covers the critical law including total variation, not just the appearance of the Bessel normalization. The subcritical limit comes from the very same theorem at parameter zero; the remaining relative concentration is the elementary single-mode ratio estimate for the known weights. There is no claim here that a prior centralizer paper literally states all three regimes.
